title: Why the Dixieland band stood out: playing in fugue form
summary: He argues the band made history because its records interweaved three distinct melodies like a conversation of instruments, an idea from opera.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What to think while improvising: wrong notes and being in the moment

blocks.x: Now, if these Negroes were so great, and they said they came to New York before me, or any other bands that came there, they never was noticed, and their music couldn't have been any different than if they were playing anywhere else in the world. But they noticed the Dixieland Jazz Band. We stood out, we made history. We played record. We're not only the pioneers, but this record, we left for posterity, a way of playing that has never been improved on to this day. The way we played was in fugue form. Any record that you pick out, I know nothing about music. I'm just a Negro scholar of music, but I went to too many operas, opera places where I could hear good music, and I seen how they played the background, the country melody, and different melodies against one another. I learned that at the French opera, when I worked down there handling lights, when I was just a male boy. I could see one person singing one tune, and another one singing against it, whether it was country melody or not. But that impressed me much in the late years that I was incorporated at. And what we had was nothing but a conversation of instruments. Well, take the liver stable blues, which I say to the clarinet, la-e-da-da, clarinet answer me, do-do-do-do-do-do. If you listen to them, three distinct melodies. Take the trombone apart, and you'll have a melody. Take the clarinet, you'll have a melody. Take the clarinet, you'll have a melody. And they're three distinct melodies working together. That is why they have never found out how nobody else could ever play the way we played, because they didn't have the idea or the scheme.
Let's see if it's working first. It sounds all right. Go ahead.
